Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a fundamental factual error in the very first step by incorrectly identifying Robert Menzies as the "founder of Australia's Liberal Party" in the context of his becoming Prime Minister in 1939. At the time he became Prime Minister (1939), Menzies was the leader of the United Australia Party (UAP). The Liberal Party of Australia was not founded until 1944. While Menzies did later become the founder of the Liberal Party, the event that caused him to become Prime Minister was the death of Joseph Lyons in 1939 while he was leading the UAP. By conflating his later role as Liberal founder with his earlier ascent to power, the Planner established a false premise that led to the subsequent agents searching for information about the "Liberal Party" in 1939, which did not exist, rather than focusing on the United Australia Party or the general leadership transition of the UAP.
